analysis:
Only CHANGELOG.md (documentation) was supplied; no code or tests, so none of the described behavior could be verified. The security-relevant claims are:
- SSD prefix cache defaults: MiMo COMPLETE-prefix checkpoints default-on (lines 324-326), Qwen3.5-9B default-on (519), and the write budget raised to 750 GB/day (430).
- The 30-minute TTL and the HMAC-keyed names match T-041, so no new finding. The per-donation demand gating (513) narrows the at-rest exposure. The unknown-ID gate (`DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE` affirmative) and the kill switch (`=0`) are consistent with T-041.
- Coordinator cache-routing persistence (389-393) stores holders and demand in the database. It states that raw hashes and prompts are not persisted. The code is not visible, so key derivation and per-account scope cannot be confirmed.
- Other claims touching existing security surfaces: T-031 removal of the earnings endpoint (487), fail-closed attestation challenges (489), App Attest protocol 3 only (491), the minimum provider version floor (483), public model-demand privacy thresholds of 20 requests and 3 accounts (559), and the bounded non-streaming response size (338).
Findings raised: the hardware-interest PII store versus T-059 (line 304), and the Connect payout/webhook cutover versus TB-008/T-030 (256). A later pass should verify the code behind these claims, especially webhook verification and idempotency, the erasure path, and the cache persistence scope.

findings.detail: The changelog adds a per-account hardware-interest table (memory/Postgres upsert) with an admin export joined to the current email. This is a new personal-data store. T-059 enumerates the data that account erasure must remove, and this store is not listed in the supplied definitions. If erasure does not delete these rows, an erased account's selection and email-linked interest can persist, and the admin export would keep returning it. Update the T-059 inventory and erasure path to cover this table, and confirm the export is admin-gated and bounded.
findings.title: Hardware-interest registry stores per-account email-joined data; erasure coverage unstated

findings.detail: The changelog introduces separate legacy Connect credentials, connected-account webhook verification distinct from Checkout, rejected-transfer refund recovery, and payout debits gated on financial-account funding. These add a webhook ingress with its own signing secret, a second settlement path for Checkout events, and a refund-repair tool. Forged or replayed webhooks, double settlement across current and legacy Checkout events, and mis-credited refunds are plausible failure modes. The existing payment threats (e.g. T-030) cover duplicate Stripe webhooks only for the original flow. Extend TB-008 and T-030 to cover the legacy-secret webhook endpoint, replay and idempotency across both paths, and operator-run refund repair. Only the changelog is visible, so the implementation was not reviewed.
findings.title: New legacy Connect webhook and payout cutover paths are not reflected in the payments threat model
